items.title: EFFORT
items.quote: A mizmor for the inauguration of the Bais HaMikdash, by David.
items.text: Learn from David’s example and do whatever you can to serve Hashem, even when you know you will not be able to see your project through to completion. It is your duty to put your efforts into doing what is right (hishtadlus), while recognizing that what ultimately happens depends on the will of Hashem.

items.title: A MEASURE OF THANKS
items.quote: I raise You on high, Hashem, for You have drawn me up.
items.text: The greater the kindness that Hashem has shown to you, the greater is your duty to show gratitude to Him.

items.title: TWOFOLD JOY
items.quote: You have not let my enemies rejoice over me.
items.text: Be grateful that the resha’im have not been given the opportunity to rejoice and that they have not been given the opportunity to enjoy the public weakening of respect for Hashem.

items.title: PERSONAL THANKS
items.quote: Hashem, my G-d, I cried out to You alone and You healed me.
items.text: In thanking Hashem, recognize your personal relationship to Him. You didn’t just get healed; it was He who healed you.

items.title: DEVOTION
items.quote: Sing to Hashem, [all of you who are] His devout ones.
items.text: It is not enough to be devout. Your devotion should encompass a strong sense of love toward Hashem. Be one of “His” devout ones.

items.title: RESPONSE
items.quote: and give thanks to His holy Name.
items.text: When you hear someone describe the miracles that Hashem has performed for him, you should respond by praising His Name.

items.title: PAST AND FUTURE
items.quote: For His anger lasts but a moment while His favor is for a lifetime.
items.text: When life seems to go against you and you find that you are experiencing the anger of Hashem, remember that His anger is short relative to the time of His good will toward you in the past. Also remember that His anger serves an important purpose. (1) It makes you appreciate how good it was to have His good will up to now. (2) It encourages you to prepare yourself for a restoration of His good will in the future.

items.title: PAST AND FUTURE
items.quote: The weeping in the evening stays overnight but there is a cry of joy in the morning.
items.text: The anguish that you experience in difficult times prepares for the joy you will feel when Hashem smiles upon you again. This includes future times of simchah in this world as well as in the World to Come.

items.title: SELF-DELUSION
items.quote: I said in my serenity, ‘I will never falter.’
items.text: When things go well for you, you may be grateful, but if that good fortune persists over a period of time, you will be tempted to believe it is your own doing or just good luck. This is a delusion. Then when things turn bad for you, you will realize that your “mountain of strength” that you thought could never falter, was actually granted by the favor of Hashem.

items.quote: Hashem, with Your favor You supported my mountain of strength..
As soon as You hid Your face I became disconcerted.
items.text: You became like a small child whose parents are hidden from him.

items.title: REACTION
items.quote: I will call to You, Hashem, I will appeal to my L-rd.
items.text: When you experience any kind of distress, your reaction should be to turn to Hashem. Recognize that the purpose of such an event is to motivate you to call to Him.

items.title: JUSTIFICATION
items.quote: What gain is there for my soul in my descent to the grave?
items.text: The basis for any appeal that you make to Hashem should not be a self-serving benefit, but to be granted an opportunity to do His will and serve Him in this life.

items.quote: Will the dust acknowledge You? Will it declare Your truth?
items.text: Although the souls in the World to Come will have the opportunity of praising Hashem in a state of unending glory, this still cannot equal the value to Hashem of a person praising Him out of his own free will in this world.

items.title: THE GIFT OF LIFE
items.quote: So that [my] soul might sing to You and not be stilled.
items.text: The true bitterness of death is not being immersed in Torah and mitzvos.

items.title: ETERNAL THANKS
items.quote: Hashem, my G-d, I will forever thank You.
items.text: A major purpose of life is the opportunity to thank Hashem. Therefore you should never waste a minute of the time when you are able to fulfill this mission. By continuing to thank Him in this world you will merit the opportunity to continue doing so in the World to Come.
